MAJOR_FINDING: The anchor absence is neither the source coverage gap phase 1 diagnosed nor a simple sparse/incomplete load. It is a county_fips MISTAGGING defect in the staged tx_building_footprint table: real, correctly-located Microsoft ML footprint rows for both probe parcels are already loaded, sitting 1.63m and 0m from the two anchors respectively, but tagged with an adjacent county's FIPS code (Lee County 48287 for the Bastrop anchor and its surrounding city; Hays County 48209 for the entire West Lake Hills city, a 100% mistagging rate there). The writer's own county-scoped candidate query (packages/engine-core/src/building-footprint/staged-footprint-join.ts:244, `ON fp.county_fips = $6`) is written correctly against the schema as documented but is blind to these rows because the STAGING step, not the join logic, assigned the wrong county. Total row volume matches the 2026-08-19 reading exactly (no drift), and the live public Microsoft source (pulled directly, no credential, this session) is dense at both anchors -- so this is not a source gap and not a volume-incomplete load. It reads as LOAD-side under the ruling's binary (fix belongs in a reload/re-tag through P-169's job against the SAME dataset; no second source), but the mechanism is narrower and more actionable than 'partial load': the county assignment must be corrected to true point/polygon containment (e.g. against tx_county_boundary, the same kind of ring/point-in-polygon method landing_parcel_jurisdiction already uses correctly on the parcel side of this program), not merely re-run with more rows.
footprintGapReadingRationale: Per the ruling's own reversal criteria and this phase's pre-registered falsifier, both keyed on 'the anchor still has no polygon within 200m': that premise is FALSE (1.63m nearest at the Bastrop anchor; 0m/contains at the West Lake Hills anchor) once measured without the county_fips-filter artifact both this phase and phase 1 initially fell into. The city-limits counts are town-appropriate in scale (Bastrop 3987, comparable Elgin 3966; independently cross-checked at 8356 via the live Microsoft tile) -- the layer is not sparse by volume. The specific, evidenced mechanism is a county_fips mistagging bug at staging, which is a load/tagging defect eligible for a corrected reload under P-169, not a case for a second-source acquisition.
falsifier: Pre-registered verbatim at CP1: 'if the count inside Bastrop city limits is within an order of magnitude of the town's building count and the anchor still has no polygon within 200 m, the load-gap reading is wrong and the source-gap reading stands.' OBSERVED: the city-limits count is town-appropriate in scale (see counts above) AND the anchor DOES have a polygon within 200m (1.63m) once the county_fips filter artifact is removed. The falsifier's trigger condition did not hold, so it did not overturn the load-gap reading; instead it surfaced the mechanism (mistagging, not mere sparsity) that phase 1's and this phase's own first-pass queries had both silently assumed away by filtering on county_fips before checking whether that filter itself was truthful.
contradicted: Phase 1's leading conclusion -- 'the dominant cause ... is a genuine ML-source coverage gap ... no code fix in this lane's scope can manufacture a nearby footprint the Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints dataset never captured' -- is FALSE for both anchor parcels, and phase 1's own headline distances (1615m for 48021:34049, 7464m for 48453:113408) were artifacts of an unstated county_fips filter, not true nearest-footprint measurements. Neither this dispatch's phase 2 text nor the 2026-09-12 ruling anticipated the specific mechanism found (cross-county mistagging of already-loaded rows); both correctly anticipated that SOME count would decide load vs source, and the count did decide it, just via a sharper mechanism than either 'sparse load' or 'source gap' as originally framed.

leave_behind: PRIMARY FINDING FOR P-169: tx_building_footprint's county_fips column is mistagged for a large share of rows near county boundaries -- confirmed for Bastrop County (48021, 50.0% of the county's true building stock correctly tagged, the rest attributed to Lee 48287 or Caldwell 48055) and total (100%) for West Lake Hills' footprints inside Travis County (48453), which are entirely attributed to Hays County (48209) instead. P-169's writer job must assign/correct county_fips by true point-or-polygon containment against tx_county_boundary (the same class of method landing_parcel_jurisdiction already applies correctly, via its 'ring' method, on the parcel side of this program) -- not whatever coarse (likely bounding-box) method produced this result, or a straight reload from the same dataset will reproduce the identical bug and both anchor parcels will remain FAIL.

Both P-158 probe parcels are extremely likely to flip from absent to present once county_fips is corrected and the writer/reconcile re-run: the Bastrop anchor's nearest true footprint is 1.63m away (would almost certainly classify as a primary attach, ratio near 1.0) and the West Lake Hills anchor's nearest footprint has distance 0 (contains the point). This is a prediction for phase 3 to verify, not a claim made from a writer run in this phase -- no writer or reconcile job was executed.

The unmerged loader branch named in phase 1 (hauska-engine feat/p2-4-tx-building-footprint-staging, e7145a3) is the most likely place the mistagging bug lives, since the mainline main-branch writer code (staged-footprint-join.ts) only ever reads county_fips, never assigns it -- assignment happens at staging/ingest time, which is that unmerged branch's job. Not opened or read this phase (out of the 'do not run the writer' scope), but flagged again for whoever builds P-169's job to inspect before reusing any of its logic.

The Microsoft dataset-links.csv manifest and the per-quadkey tile the Bastrop anchor falls in (RegionName=UnitedStates, quadkey=023130123, ~7.6MB gzipped, ~82777 features) are reachable live with no credential -- useful as a fast, free cross-check for any future county's coverage question before anyone considers buying a second source.
